lines.speaker: wren
lines.text: Threads first, because everything else is built on them. Bandwidth is how many threads you get at the start of your turn. Most actions cost one. The heavy ones cost two or three.

lines.speaker: wren
lines.text: Keep one back and it banks as Slack, up to two — so a quiet turn is not a wasted turn. Next turn you act with more than you were given.

lines.speaker: wren
lines.text: Tempo is the gauge between us. Every thread any of us spends puts two points in it, and it holds forty. It belongs to the party, not to me, whatever Dax tells you.

lines.speaker: wren
lines.text: It is the only thing in this century that gets easier the harder we work, so do not hoard it. A full gauge you never spend is a fight you fought the ordinary way.

lines.speaker: wren
lines.text: Three Tempo buys a Rewind. The last thing an enemy did to us comes undone, and they take that turn again and do something else with it. I can manage one a battle. A second anchor, or the right training, buys another.

lines.speaker: wren
lines.text: Two Tempo and one thread buys a Fork. You see precisely what an action would do — the number, the shield, who goes down — and then you decide whether to do it. It is not an estimate. It is the same future, read twice.

lines.speaker: wren
lines.text: And every time we pull, Entropy rises. Twenty for a Rewind. Ten for a Fork. More for anything Chronal.

lines.speaker: wren
lines.text: Past seventy it answers back. An Echo of one of us steps out of a version of the fight we did not have — your face, my voice, standing on the wrong side — and nothing but Chronal damage will touch it.

lines.speaker: wren
lines.text: That is the whole bargain, Auditor. Time will give you the turn back. It simply wants to be paid in versions of yourself.
